title: hoa_fined_me_for_grass_height
beats: My HOA president fined me $200 for 'grass over 4 inches' — measured with her own kitchen ruler.
I'm 31M, I work from home, and I mow every single Saturday like clockwork.
She's not on the board's measurement committee. She's not on any committee. She just walks around with a ruler and a grudge.
So I paid the fine, smiled, and asked for a copy of the official HOA turf-height policy in writing.
Buried on page 47: all measurements must be conducted by a licensed board inspector using calibrated equipment, with 48 hours written notice.
She'd violated her own bylaws eleven times this year alone, all documented in her smug little fine letters.
I filed a formal grievance with the state HOA regulatory board and attached every single one.
Two weeks later she got fined $200 for 'unauthorized enforcement action' — same exact number she charged me.
Then the board suspended her enforcement privileges for six months pending review.
Last Saturday I watched her drive past my lawn, slow down, grip her ruler... and keep driving.
So, was I wrong for saving every receipt just to hand her the bill?
